notes:
Account background:
- Legacy national broadcaster with 25+ years of archived articles, transcripts, and raw multimedia captions. Content set uneven: lots of very long transcripts (20k+ tokens) and OCR'd legacy documents with noisy text.
- Primary goal: fast, high-quality search over archives for newsroom workflows + editorial research. Secondary: programmatic summarization for content packages.

Business / constraints:
- Must keep primary index in NA region; legal asked for partial residency for European subset. Considering Redwood Dedicated (VPC) for SLA + residency controls.
- Cost sensitivity: editorial searches ~300k queries/month, acceptable ARR mid-market band but wants clear cost-per-query models.

Technical requirements discussed:
- Indexing scale: target initial index ~28M chunks (estimated after chunking), long-term 100M+. Need benchmarks for 100M vector index ops and memory sizing guidance.
- Chunking strategy: team prefers semantic chunks ~800-1200 tokens with 200 token overlap for context continuity. Concern: shorter chunks increase recall but spike candidate volume for reranker. Want Redwood recommendations: chunk size tradeoffs vs tokenization + KV cache impact.
- Embedding model preference: open models initially (sentence-transformer family) but open to Redwood-verified cased models. Must support incremental re-embedding pipeline for daily ingests.
- Reranker plan: cross-encoder reranker for top-K re-rank (K=50 default). Latency SLO for interactive use: 300ms p95 for search-only paths; 600ms p95 when reranker enabled. Need Redwood guidance on batching/cross-encoder offloading and GPU sizing.
- Candidate recall / precision targets: recall@50 >= 0.90 on curated eval set; nDCG improvements over baseline embedding-only retrieval > 0.12. Want to tie regressions to prompt-evals in Redwood Optimize.

POC summary / timeline:
- 2025-11-12: Intro call; AE/SE mapped requirements (ff_20260115_5467).
- 2025-12-02: Provided sample dataset (3M chunks) and eval prompt set (600 queries).
- 2026-01-10: Initial hosted API proof — embedding-only search on 3M chunks; recall ~0.78 at 50, avg latency 180ms excluding rerank.
- 2026-01-15: Meeting to discuss reranker approach (ff_20260115_5467). Decided to test cross-encoder candidate size 50 then 30.
- 2026-02-10: Security questionnaire submitted; security call with infra (ff_20260210_8892). Legal flagged EU residency for subset.
- 2026-02-18: Deployed dedicated POC pool (4xA100 equivalent) for reranker tuning; initial 24h run showed reranker p95 ~820ms for K=50 (too high).

Notes from SE / tuning playbook (shorthand):
- Try 1) reduce chunk overlap to 100 tokens and increase chunk size to 1k tokens -> reduces candidate count but may drop recall on short-span queries. Run ablation.
- Try 2) hybrid recall: FAISS HNSW for recall retrieval (top-200) then embed-similarity for initial prune -> feed cross-encoder on top-30. Might save reranker work.
- Try 3) quantized reranker on mixed precision or smaller cross-encoder (distilled) as fallback for low-latency routes. Use Redwood Optimize to model cost vs quality tradeoff.
- Batching: continuous batching for reranker inefficient for interactive; test micro-batching (batch sizes 4-8) on dedicated pool to hit p95 targets.
- Caching: implement prefix/KV caching for long sessions (editor searches often iterative). Chart expected token savings and cost.

- "If reranker doubles our costs per query we need a clear fallback policy."
